signals.evidence: Abihai Stern, mayor of Kiryat Shmona: 'The current discussion is about formulating a national compensation framework for all business owners in Israel, and is not focused only on the north.' He was told he could not join via Zoom.
Tzala Weiss (50), writing workshop facilitator: 'The war brought us business owners to the edge... I opened the business 11 years ago and never thought it would be harmed - it's my baby.'

Rambam Hospital received 10 IDF soldiers wounded in clash with Hezbollah operatives in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon. Three wounded severely, one moderately, six lightly. Since Operation Saar HaAri began, hospital received 87 wounded soldiers plus hundreds of civilians injured from missile strikes.

Northern residents followed negotiations in Washington with skepticism, under rocket and drone barrages. Despite PM Netanyahu's declaration that the goal is peace with Lebanon, the reality in the north appears far from it. Hezbollah barrages indicate an organization that will struggle greatly to abandon its aspirations.

State Comptroller report (January 2026): In hospitals near the border, 67% of imaging devices, 48% of hospital beds, 25% of ICU beds, and 22% of operating rooms are unprotected. Nearly half of hospital beds are transferred to alternative sites in emergency.

Abihai Stern, mayor of Kiryat Shmona: 'In the last three years I have participated, together with other local authority heads, more than once in Knesset committee Zoom meetings. In practice, behind the washing of words, the committee chair refuses to hear from representatives of the public about problems and gaps, and refuses to promote discourse adapted to days of battle with elected representatives of the authorities.'

Ten alerts activated in the north within two hours; reports of two impact sites in Nahariya. MDA: no casualties. IDF announced possible increased fire from Lebanon in coming hours, likely toward the north.

Diaspora Ministry report: 20 Jews murdered in antisemitic incidents in the past year, including 15 in a deadly attack in Australia. Report reveals social media platforms (Meta, X, TikTok) became central engine for spreading 'fake news' and AI-based antisemitism.

CyberWell and FOA reports: Holocaust denial and distortion not only persisted but became viral due to widespread use of AI and coded language. Example: animated trailer in Pixar style called 'Caust' created with tools like Sora or Veo3, making Holocaust accessible as entertainment for children while praising Hitler and mocking victims, using memes and songs to evade platform detection mechanisms.

David Azulai: 'We had a relatively quiet night from both sides. There are those who say there will be escalation, in fact we see relative quiet since yesterday evening. This lights a red light for me. We want security here because that is the only thing I think can bring back the communities, young families, and we must have security. This has been lacking here for decades. We are tired of wars. We are two and a half years into war. We are tired. We need quiet.'

Abihai Stern, mayor of Kiryat Shmona: 'I did not leave Kiryat Shmona, and you will not escape my criticism.' Stern stated he tried to attend the Finance Committee discussion on compensation framework but was not permitted to join remotely, despite the city being under continuous bombardment.

Ten IDF soldiers wounded in Bint Jbeil: three severely, two moderately, five lightly. Paratroopers unit encountered Hezbollah operatives at close range during clearing operations. Wounded evacuated by helicopter to Rambam Hospital in Haifa.

Operation Saar HaAri placed Holocaust survivors in impossible security reality, but government response remained slow and cumbersome. Special committee discussions in March 2026 revealed no complete mapping of shelter infrastructure for elderly and Holocaust survivors. Older survivors lack accessible housing providing proper protection adapted to their needs.

During Paratroopers unit activity in Bint Jbeil, forces encountered three operatives who opened fire. In rapid response, soldiers returned fire; with tank fire and air strikes, two operatives were eliminated and the building was attacked. Three IDF soldiers wounded severely, one moderately, six lightly. A third operative attempting to flee was located and eliminated.

Shira Shagev: 'It's moving on every level. We believed it would happen but not so fast... It's a great privilege to step here and drive on the roads again.' Adi Galbert: 'There are challenges but when you see the spirit is very strong the challenges shrink. There's something very natural here. The children are happy and joyful, there's something basic, special and powerful.'
Evacuees returning to Sha'ar Nur settlement; children playing and running in streets; families settling in temporary caravans; community resuming normal activities despite physical constraints

Female soldier: 'Surrounded by enemies, facing my eyes Dura, El Fawwar and all the villages around - and meanwhile life in this small settlement continues... I stop for a moment and think who is guarding whom?'
Soldier protecting settlement residents; residents blessing soldier with 'Happy holiday' and 'Thank you'; note on wall saying 'Thank you for guarding us'

Kinneret beaches opened to public following Home Front Command easing of restrictions; first visitors and vacationers arrived; soldiers from Lebanon and youth from the valley came to camp and enjoy the lake
Actress Aliana Tadhar: 'Today the siren mixed for me with the alerts... I need to explain to my son Nevo in the future that the siren is not a call to shelter, but a cry of a broken heart.'

IDF Spokesperson issued unusual warning of possible massive rocket fire from Lebanon toward Israel, likely targeting the north. IDF calls on residents, especially those in confrontation line and north, to maintain high alertness, show vigilance, act responsibly and follow Home Front Command guidelines.

Home Front Command announced defense policy guidelines will remain unchanged and in effect until Sunday, April 19, 2026, 20:00. Detailed restrictions by region: confrontation line - limited activity, educational activities only in protected spaces; Golan North, Upper Galilee - limited activity with protected space access during alerts; other regions - gathering limits of 5,000 people.
Nature reserve inspector reports that the vast majority of rescue cases involve yeshiva students; students ignoring professional field guidelines and safety instructions from reserve rangers

Nine yeshiva students rescued from two complex rescue operations in Judean Desert: three cliff rappellers trapped at 72-meter waterfall in Nahal Tamrim after rope broke; six hikers lost in Nahal Draga after entering closed wadi, found exhausted after hours in difficult terrain

Approximately 30 volunteers from Gilot rescue unit operated in field from evening to early morning hours; rescue operation included police helicopter assisting in locating missing persons and evacuations; volunteers conducted foot searches across kilometers in difficult terrain and complete darkness
FlyDubai airline announced return to operations in Israel starting Thursday of the coming week, initially operating two daily flights between Ben Gurion and Dubai
Wizz Air announced suspension of all flights to and from Israel through May 4

Holocaust survivor Irene Shasha: 'I stand here today as the sole representative of my siblings, with dozens of officers and commanders of the IDF, whose people embody the essence of strength and human dignity. From here I send you a promise: we will continue to march with pride, together. Despite all obstacles, our will and spirit carry us forward - together, unbreakable. Am Yisrael Chai!' Lt. Col. Gai Hason: 'We are standing here together - connecting past, present and future... The memory obligates us to act, to be strong and to be united.'

Hostage Omri Miran: 'During my captivity I thought a lot about my grandmother and grandfather who managed to survive one of the darkest periods humanity has known. My grandmother and grandfather insisted on turning their national and personal tragedy into new lives - they built a family, built the country. Full of values and Zionism... Just here today - I want to remind us of this duty. Like the generations before us, we too must rise together.'

Healthcare system experiencing new burden from Home Front Command restrictions: temporary clinic closures, reduced surgeries, halted procedures, frozen elective operations. Long waiting times for doctors, surgeries, and tests already existed; new restrictions push system backward. Even months of diagnostic delay can affect recovery chances.

Ministry of Education issued unprecedented directive requiring school principals to report daily to ministry on student grades, behavior, absences, and disciplinary issues. Directive was distributed by external vendor without ministry coordination or approval. After backlash, ministry claimed directive was issued without authorization and was immediately removed, but instructions to principals stated explicitly it was Ministry of Education requirement.

Petah Tikva Mayor Rami Greenberg to Education Minister: high school students facing emotional and academic difficulties from war - disrupted routine, prolonged absences, psychological burden. Requested reducing external matriculation exams to core subjects only (Hebrew, Math, English, one elective), with other subjects assessed internally; reduce exam material scope; expand accommodations for fair testing conditions.

Self-Employed Organization head Roy Cohen: 'We are seven weeks into the war, and not a single shekel of compensation has reached business owners and self-employed.' Stated government failure in handling emergency compensation, demanded permanent framework automatically triggered during emergency declaration, expanded compensation for small self-employed and sectors hit hardest (tourism, culture, events).

Chamber of Commerce Federation head Shahar Turgeman: 'The private sector is the generator that produces the current - without it there is no hope for the battery... The state must invest in the private sector because it's an investment that returns itself many times over.' Noted 65,000 businesses closed or went bankrupt in 2025, 61,000 in 2024 - negative balance.

Arab communities in Israel face acute shortage of shelters and protected spaces, making them more vulnerable than other areas. Only 0.3% of public shelters in Israel are located in Arab communities due to lack of public land. Educational institutions in Arab communities cannot access fortification budgets because most school buildings are on private land.

Metula Mayor David Azoulay: 'They don't update us on why the rules were eased. Maybe they know something we don't.' - expressing confusion about lack of explanation for Home Front Command guideline changes

IDF reservist Eyal Uriel Bianco, age 30, killed when Humvee overturned in southern Lebanon. Three other reservists injured: one moderately, two lightly. Bianco was a firefighter driver in the 188 Barak Brigade, served hundreds of reserve days since start of war on February 28.

Ten IDF soldiers from Paratroopers Brigade wounded in clash with Hezbollah in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon: three seriously wounded, one moderately, six lightly. All evacuated to hospitals, families notified.

Holocaust Remembrance Day siren sounded throughout Israel; country came to standstill; drivers halted cars on highways, pedestrians remained silent and unmoving. Main state ceremony held at Yad Vashem with PM Netanyahu, President Herzog, IDF Chief of Staff, and Holocaust survivors attending.

IDF warns of possible increased Hezbollah rocket attacks and states 'civilians should maintain vigilance' and 'If there are changes in the situational assessment, the public will be updated accordingly'
Sirens have been sounding across the Galilee for the past half an hour, warning of rocket fire from Lebanon

Home Front Command says wartime guidelines remain unchanged until Sunday night; educational activities permitted only inside bomb shelters in communities on Lebanon border; gatherings restricted to 5,000 in some areas of north, 1,000 in others

Sergeant Major (Res.) Ayal Uriel Bianco, 30-year-old fire truck driver in 188th Brigade from Katzrin, was killed during combat in southern Lebanon; one reservist moderately wounded, two others sustained light injuries

Noam Nov of Amitim for Rights: 'the mind and body don't switch off on command' and describes sharp transitions from shelters to work, children sleeping in parking lots then preparing for exams as 'not normal'
Ten soldiers wounded in fighting in southern Lebanon overnight, including three in serious condition, one moderate, six light wounds; all evacuated to hospitals
Rambam Health Care Campus helipad received casualties from fighting in Lebanon; ten IDF soldiers wounded in clash, three seriously, evacuated to Rambam and other northern hospitals

Ten IDF soldiers from Paratroopers Brigade wounded in close-quarters confrontation with Hezbollah in Bint Jbeil; three severely wounded, one moderately, six minor injuries; complex evacuation mission conducted

IDF warns of possibility that Hezbollah will significantly increase attacks on Israel; public should remain vigilant and adhere to Home Front Command protective guidelines; 'IDF is prepared to operate both defensively and offensively'

Commander of Battalion 52, Lt. Col. 'A.', seriously wounded during operational activity in southern Lebanon; ten soldiers wounded in encounter—three seriously, one moderately, six lightly; all evacuated to hospital
